title: The biomechanics of better bras: improving support and comfort during exercise
publisher: International Society of Biomechanics in Sports (ISBS) Conference Proceedings
claims: Female breasts contain no substantial anatomical support apart from the skin and fine hair-like Cooper's ligaments, so breast tissue moves relatively freely over the chest wall during activities with vertical trunk movement such as running.

As little as 2 cm of vertical breast displacement is sufficient to induce breast discomfort in some females, and women with large breasts can experience more than 10 cm of breast displacement during running without adequate support.
Studies have found that up to 100% of women were wearing the wrong size bra.
Poor bra fit has been linked with upper limb neural symptoms, deep bra furrows from excessive strap pressure, non-cyclical mastalgia, and neck and back pain.

In a survey of 267 Australian women (mean age 27.2 years), only 41% wore an encapsulating sports bra when participating in physical activity; the most disliked features were shoulder straps cutting in and straps slipping off the shoulders.
A correctly fitted sports bra did not significantly affect maximal exercise performance, nor respiratory function during submaximal exercise, compared with a fashion bra or no bra.
Changing shoulder straps from a traditional vertical alignment to a crossed-back configuration reduced straps slipping off the shoulders without decreasing overall breast support.
Commercially available bra strap cushions were not effective in reducing bra shoulder strap pressure in the cited study.

Among 74 breast cancer survivors, 70.3% reported experiencing bra discomfort during exercise, and 'I can't find a bra that is comfortable to exercise in' ranked fourth out of 34 perceived barriers to exercise.
In a later online survey of 482 breast cancer survivors, not being able to find a comfortable bra to exercise in was one of the top three barriers to exercise.
